subject: Next steps — deployment & migration preferences (Atlas Health)
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.inference>
To: Laura Chen <laura@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + decision inputs we need

Hi Laura — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the things we need from your side to align the next steps so we can scope a pilot: 

Call summary (quick):
- Primary use case: clinical note summarization + triage routing for urgent consults.
- Expected weekdays peak QPS: 1200 short requests (~150 tokens avg) with spiky bursts during rounds.
- Current stack: using an older on-prem GPU cluster (NVIDIA V100), plus a small pilot on another LLM API for inference.

Open qualification items we discussed (please confirm):
1) Deployment preference: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem — you mentioned predictable latency was important; can you confirm whether Atlas prefers Reserved (Dedicated) capacity for guaranteed throughput, or a Private VPC for PHI/data residency?
2) Migration complexity: if you move from the legacy GPU cluster, do you plan a lift-and-shift (containerized model artifacts) or a rebuild onto our model catalog and runtime? Any blockers for us connecting to your cluster during a POC?
3) Security/compliance: you asked about SOC2 evidence & network topology — attaching a short SOC2-summary. What additional artifacts will procurement need?

Proposed next steps / asks (mutual action plan draft attached):
- Please confirm deployment preference (Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC) and any hard constraints (VPC peering only, no egress, specific KMS).
- Share the procurement contact and estimated timeline for a 3–6 month POC.
- If you want a technical deep-dive: propose two 60-min slots next week and we’ll bring runtime and infra leads.

Attachments: MAP_AtlasHealth_v1.pdf (mutual action plan, draft), SOC2-summary.pdf (summary and SOC2 report redaction guidance).

I’m looping Rishi and Priyom for pricing/contract and infra questions.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura@atlashealth.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement <procure@atlashealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + decision inputs we need

Thanks Aisha — great session. Quick answers inline and a few specifics from procurement below.

On Sun, 1 Aug 2026 at 14:03, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.inference> wrote:
> 1) Deployment preference: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem — you mentioned predictable latency was important; can you confirm whether Atlas prefers Reserved (Dedicated) capacity for guaranteed throughput, or a Private VPC for PHI/data residency?

We are leaning toward Dedicated capacity initially for predictable throughput and to avoid burst throttling while we validate latency SLAs. However, because we handle PHI (covered under our BAAs), we will require either: (a) Dedicated in a VPC with strict network controls, or (b) Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) if the legal team pushes back. We’ll need to confirm after procurement reviews the contract.

> 2) Migration complexity: if you move from the legacy GPU cluster, do you plan a lift-and-shift (containerized model artifacts) or a rebuild onto our model catalog and runtime? Any blockers for us connecting to your cluster during a POC?

Short term: we want a lift-and-shift path to speed POC (we have containerized model weights and an entrypoint that matches OpenAPI calls). Long term we’re open to onboarding a Redwood model variant if it reduces ops overhead. We can open firewall rules for a timeboxed connection during the POC; IT will need an IP allowlist and an SA.

Procurement notes (procure@atlashealth.ai):
- POC contract target: 60 days.
- Required documents: SOC2 (attestation), data processing addendum, vendor security questionnaire.
- Billing: prefer net-30 on POC invoice; procurement will confirm credit terms.

Timeline: procurement will respond with final T&Cs by 3 Aug. If that lands OK, we can start a tech deep-dive week of Aug 9.

Best —
Laura Chen
Director, AI Platforms
Atlas Health
laura@atlashealth.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura@atlashealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap + decision inputs we need

Looping in technical asks and pricing implications. Notes from my side: 
- If Atlas elects Dedicated + VPC peering: estimate capacity for 1200 QPS peak is ~6 x A100-equivalents in dedicated pool for target p95 < 200ms for 150-token responses. Pricing will be a reserved monthly commitment; we will prepare two commitment tiers (baseline + burst).
- If Atlas requires Private deployment: we’ll need lead time for VPC onboarding and KMS integration (2–4 weeks), and a different license/enterprise contract.
- Lift-and-shift POC path: we can accept the containerized entrypoint — we’ll run a compatibility test during the technical deep-dive. Firewall/IP allowlist and a short-term VPN or temporary peering are fine.

Action items I’ll cover:
1) Draft two pricing scenarios (Dedicated-committed vs Dedicated-with-burst) by EOD Wed (4 Aug).
2) Prepare a short tech checklist for the POC (network, KMS, model packaging, metrics hooks).
3) Coordinate with legal on DPA/SOC2 artifacts — ask: who is the procurement contact? (Laura, can you confirm the right person for contract redlines?)

Proposed times for technical deep-dive week of Aug 9 (PT):
- Tue 10 Aug 09:00–10:00 PT (runtime + infra)
- Wed 11 Aug 14:00–15:00 PT (runtime + security)

I’ll hold both tentatively.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
